meetings.headline: Cemetery Commission held burial and lot fees steady, hired flower care, and approved up to $200 for dump-deterrent cameras.
meetings.summary: The Cemetery Commission heard a resident's request about holiday decorations, thanked DPW seasonal help, and reviewed neighboring towns' burial rates. It decided to keep lot and burial fees unchanged, voted to pay for flower care in 2022, to buy back a returned lot, and to buy cameras to deter dumping.

budget_items.what_was_said: Chair described current burial fee structure and lot sale split between the sale-of-lots account and perpetual care; burial fees go to the town. Commission chose not to raise lot or burial fees.
figures_as_heard: four hundred dollars for the lot
two hundred dollars for perpetual care

budget_items.topic: Flower planting and care contract for 2022
budget_items.what_was_said: A local contractor quoted a yearly price for care of flowers at both cemeteries, excluding plant costs. Commission voted to pay it.

budget_items.topic: SIMS software annual cost and update
budget_items.what_was_said: Chair said the commission currently spends about eighteen hundred dollars yearly on the system for hosting and maintenance; an optional update was deferred for further review.
A lot owner who moved away asked the commission to buy back two lots; the buy-back refunds the price minus perpetual care, with hope to resell at a higher price.
Commission authorized spending up to a set amount on two game cameras to deter dumping, with the cemetery superintendent buying and being reimbursed.
Seasonal DPW help for the cemeteries was praised and expected to be funded again next year via the town manager's budget.

decisions.decision: Commission agreed to hold off on raising lot and burial fees for now and revisit later, looking for other ways to raise money.
The SIMS software update will be re-reviewed at a future meeting; the email will be resent to the member.
The chair will draft a thank-you letter from the commission to the DPW director for the seasonal help and circulate it.
The chair will check with the cemetery superintendent whether the owners still want the buy-back and raise the idea of holding the lots for hardship cases.
The chair will draft a Facebook post reminding the public of cemetery decoration rules and share it with members.
Commission will take under consideration a trial of seasonal Christmas decoration rules and discuss it with the DPW.

budget_items.what_was_said: Grant money secured by the town manager has a June deadline, so the project must go to bid or quotes soon; an extension may be requested.
Commission recommended appropriating a sum from the sale of lots account at town meeting to fund operating costs and fieldstones for the Goodrich yard wall.
Powell Construction's grading, crushed asphalt and loam work will be paid after July 1.
Hydroseeding by Lakeview is to be paid shortly from the current appropriation.
Chair reviewed line by line the vouchers for donuts and pizza for students, lumber and roofing, doors, electrical, siding reimbursed to Monty Tech, and a dumpster.
A sign for the new building was approved for payment with the vouchers.
The commission has a small balance left until July, with the hydroseeding to come out of it; the project finished roughly on budget.
The town now provides an annual maintenance budget for outsourced work like hedges and tree cutting.

Chair will draft a thank-you letter to Monty Tech and look into whether the commission can donate to the program.
Next meeting tentatively moved from May 20 to the week after so the incoming member can be sworn in.

why_it_matters: The new cemetery building was built with Monty Tech student labor and came in roughly on budget, so its cost is largely settled and paid from the current appropriation.
The parking lot work depends on grant money with a June deadline, and a missed deadline could mean the town pays for it some other way.
watch_next: The parking lot bid or quotes, or a grant extension request, before the June deadline.
